title: MCI — DCAS MCI Course Exam (Exam 1)
description: DCAS MCI course exam for new medics (105 questions): triage, START/RPM, triage tags, sector officers, command, staging, HAZMAT and DCAS resources.

questions.text: The use of the triage tag during an MCI is the sole responsibility of the:
questions.explanation: Tagging is the Triage Officer's job; the Treatment Officer re-triages, the Transport Officer moves patients.
questions.hint: Tagging happens during the first sort of the patients. Which officer runs that sort?

questions.text: Which is most important?
questions.explanation: Personal safety comes first — an injured rescuer becomes another casualty.
questions.hint: If you get hurt, you become one more casualty and one less rescuer.

questions.text: The first step for you to do in triage is:
options: Take care of the worst-looking victim
questions.explanation: START begins with a voice command so the walking wounded move to a set point; the remaining patients are then assessed one by one. Stopping to look, listen and think belongs to the scene size-up before triage starts.
questions.hint: START begins with a single instruction to the whole crowd, before you touch anyone.

questions.text: You conduct voice triage:
options: To separate the males from the females
To separate victims who have a hearing difficulty/disability
To separate out the victims who are able to ambulate on their own
To separate the athletes from the stage actors
questions.explanation: Directing everyone who can walk to a set point quickly sorts out the walking wounded (GREEN).
questions.hint: What does asking everyone to walk to a set point quickly tell you about them?

questions.text: In RPM, what does P relate to?
questions.explanation: P = Perfusion, assessed by radial pulse or capillary refill (< 2 s).
questions.hint: P is for perfusion. How do you check it in seconds at a fingertip?

questions.text: In the START memorization rhyme (30 – 2 – Can do), what does "can do" relate to?
questions.explanation: 30 = respirations, 2 = capillary refill seconds, Can do = follows simple commands (mental status).
questions.hint: 30 is the breathing rate and 2 is the refill time. The third check asks the patient to do something simple.

questions.text: Which is a part of dealing with bleeding during triage?
questions.explanation: During triage you only stop life-threatening haemorrhage (direct pressure or tourniquet). Bandaging and wound care wait for the treatment area.
questions.hint: During triage you only do what saves a life in seconds. Which option is truly life-saving?

questions.text: Which is a part of dealing with broken bones during triage?
options: Remove jewelry before the part starts to swell
questions.explanation: Triage is a 30–60 second sort; splinting and other fracture care are left to the treatment area.
questions.hint: Fracture care takes time. Does it happen during the triage sort, or later?

questions.text: It is imperative that you remove/retain this portion of the triage tag when considering transportation to a hospital not equipped to handle such cases, or to better prepare the receiving hospital:
questions.explanation: The contaminated section warns the destination so a contaminated patient is not sent to an unprepared facility.
questions.hint: Which condition must a hospital prepare for before the patient arrives, and might not be able to handle at all?

questions.text: During triaging, if you are to upgrade a patient's priority, you are to:
options: Remove the lowest portion of your triage tag
Dispose of the old tag and provide a new tag
Inform the Incident Commander so he can call for backup
questions.explanation: Tear-off tags are upgraded by removing the lower colour strip(s) so the higher priority shows.
questions.hint: Tear-off tags show the priority by the colour strip left at the bottom.

questions.text: When a patient's condition improves during an MCI, what are you going to do to his/her triage tag?
options: Remove the lowest portion of your triage tag
Dispose of the old tag and provide a new tag
Keep the old triage tag and attach it with the new one
questions.explanation: Torn strips can't be re-attached, so a new tag is applied while the old one is kept with it as a record.
questions.hint: Torn strips can't be put back, but the record of the first triage still matters.

questions.text: What is the tool first responders and medical personnel use to segregate patients during an MCI?
questions.explanation: Triage tags record priority colour and travel with the patient.
questions.hint: It travels with the patient and shows their priority colour.

questions.text: Triage is a French word which means:
questions.explanation: From the French "trier" — to sort.
questions.hint: Triage puts patients into groups by priority. Which word describes that?

questions.text: Refers to an event that overwhelms the local healthcare system, with a number of casualties that vastly exceeds the local resources and capabilities in a short period of time:
questions.explanation: An MCI is defined by casualties exceeding available resources.
questions.hint: Only one option names an event by the gap between casualties and the resources available.

questions.text: DCAS Disaster Bus-C can accommodate how many patients?
questions.explanation: Bus-A: 15, Bus-B: 25, Bus-C: 33.
questions.hint: The buses get bigger from A to C, and Bus C is the largest.

questions.text: DCAS Disaster Bus-A can accommodate how many patients?
questions.explanation: Bus-A: 15, Bus-B: 25, Bus-C: 33.
questions.hint: The buses get bigger from A to C, and Bus A is the smallest.

questions.text: DCAS Disaster Bus-B can accommodate how many patients?
questions.explanation: Bus-A: 15, Bus-B: 25, Bus-C: 33.
questions.hint: Bus B sits in the middle: bigger than Bus A, smaller than Bus C.

questions.text: The triage tag is mainly used during:
questions.explanation: Triage tags are an MCI tool.
questions.hint: Tags are needed when there are too many patients to track from memory.

questions.text: In an MCI, who is responsible for communicating with dispatch about which hospitals patients will be transported to?
questions.explanation: The Transport Officer coordinates destinations with dispatch/hospitals.
questions.hint: Which officer decides where each ambulance is heading?

questions.text: Which sector officer is responsible for sorting and segregating all victims?
questions.explanation: Sorting = triage.
questions.hint: Sorting patients is the literal meaning of one officer's title.

questions.text: Any event that is expected to lead to an unstable and dangerous situation is called a:
questions.explanation: A crisis is an event expected to lead to an unstable, dangerous situation.
questions.hint: This word describes a situation that is still developing, not one that has already caused the damage.

questions.text: A sudden accident or natural catastrophe that causes great damage or loss of life is a:
questions.explanation: That is the definition of a disaster.
questions.hint: This term describes the event together with the damage and loss of life it has already caused.

questions.text: What is the immediate or urgent movement of people away from the threat or actual hazard?
questions.explanation: Evacuation is the organised, urgent movement of people away from a hazard.
questions.hint: It's the organised term emergency plans use for moving people out of danger.

questions.text: DCAS ISUZU support units are located in:
questions.explanation: ISUZU support units are based at Hatta and Jebel Ali.
questions.hint: Isnad 4 and Isnad 5 are the ISUZU units: one is in the mountains, the other by the port.

questions.text: The DCAS DELTA support unit is located in:
questions.explanation: DELTA support unit: Warsan.
questions.hint: DELTA (Isnad 3) shares its base with the MAN unit, inland east of the city.

questions.text: The DCAS MAN support unit is located in:
questions.explanation: MAN support unit: Warsan.
questions.hint: MAN (Isnad 2) shares its base with the DELTA unit, inland east of the city.

questions.text: Which sector officer is in charge of coordinating with other responding agencies?
questions.explanation: The Incident Commander coordinates with other agencies/stakeholders (per the DCAS IC checklist).
questions.hint: Other agencies need one EMS point of contact who sees the whole incident.

questions.text: Monitors workplace activities to ensure that medics comply with safety procedures:
questions.explanation: The Safety Officer monitors operations for hazards and compliance.
questions.hint: Which officer's whole job is watching for hazards and unsafe practice?

questions.text: Triage which victim first?
questions.explanation: Start where you stand — triage the nearest victim and work outward systematically.
questions.hint: Working systematically beats chasing the loudest or the worst-looking patient.

questions.text: In METHANE, N stands for:
questions.explanation: METHANE: Major incident, Exact location, Type, Hazards, Access, Number of casualties, Emergency services.
questions.hint: METHANE tells dispatch how big a response to send.

questions.text: In triaging, how long will you spend triaging a patient?
questions.explanation: START triage should take under a minute per patient.
questions.hint: Triage is a quick sort, not an assessment. Think seconds, not minutes.

questions.text: Example of a natural disaster:
questions.explanation: All are natural disasters.
questions.hint: Check each option: is it caused by nature or by people?

questions.text: Types of hazardous material/hazards:
questions.explanation: All may pose hazards to life, property or environment.
questions.hint: Could each option harm life, property or the environment?

questions.text: In staging, what is the proper/ideal distance between tarp and tarp?
questions.explanation: Tarps are laid 5 m apart.
questions.hint: Leave room for stretchers and staff to move between the tarps, more than a couple of steps.

questions.text: In staging, what is the proper/ideal distance between backboard and backboard?
questions.explanation: Backboards are placed 1 m apart.
questions.hint: Leave just enough room for one medic to kneel between two patients.

questions.text: In the SLUDGEM part of the triage tag, D stands for:
questions.explanation: SLUDGEM: Salivation, Lacrimation, Urination, Defecation, GI upset, Emesis, Miosis.
questions.hint: SLUDGEM lists the body fluids and functions a nerve agent sets off.

questions.text: The GOAL of DCAS Crisis and Disaster creation is:
questions.explanation: The division exists for readiness and preparedness.
questions.hint: The division's work starts long before any incident happens.

questions.text: The primary goal of TRIAGE in a mass casualty incident is to:
options: Ensure that all victims have immediate access to medical care
Treat and release the patient immediately
Do the most good for the greatest number of potential survivors
Notify the receiving facilities of the total number of casualties
questions.explanation: Triage rations scarce resources to save the most lives.
questions.hint: With too few resources, triage aims to save as many lives as possible rather than treat everyone at once.

questions.text: At an MCI scene, you find a man walking with two fingers amputated and several fingers severely crushed. He follows commands. The most appropriate category is:
questions.explanation: In START, anyone who can walk is initially GREEN.
questions.hint: In START, the very first question is whether the patient can walk.

questions.text: What would be collected in the STAGING AREA?
options: Patients who need to be triaged
Supplies and members of the media
questions.explanation: Staging holds incoming resources — people, vehicles, equipment — until assigned.
questions.hint: Staging holds incoming resources until the Incident Commander assigns them.

questions.text: This is the location from which the Incident Commander oversees all operations:
questions.explanation: The ICP is the on-scene command location.
questions.hint: It's on scene, not the off-site centre, and it isn't where resources wait.

questions.text: An emergency incident that produces a number of casualties and/or a severity of injuries exceeding the capacity of the initial crew or crews, preventing effective management and transport:
questions.explanation: Exceeding the initial crews' capacity defines a multiple casualty incident.
questions.hint: This definition is measured against the first crews on scene, not the whole health system.

questions.text: What is the only position that is always staffed in every incident?
questions.explanation: Every incident has an Incident Commander.
questions.hint: Even a single-ambulance call has someone in charge.

questions.text: Gold command is considered:
questions.explanation: Gold = strategic, Silver = tactical, Bronze = operational.
questions.hint: Gold, Silver and Bronze run from the big picture down to the hands-on work.

questions.text: In a HAZMAT incident, when do patients need to be decontaminated?
options: Prior to entering the treatment area
After they are treated on the scene
questions.explanation: Decontamination is done in the warm zone before patients enter the clean treatment area. A quick initial triage may happen before decontamination to set its order.
questions.hint: Keep the clean treatment area clean.

questions.text: You find a patient at the scene of a mass casualty event with a severe head injury, a pulse of 10 bpm, and he is apneic. Under the triage system he is classified as:
questions.explanation: Apneic with a non-survivable injury = expectant/deceased.
questions.hint: In START, what happens to a patient who still isn't breathing after the airway is opened?

questions.text: Which do you NOT do during triage?
questions.explanation: Triage is limited to airway opening, bleeding control and positioning.
questions.hint: Triage interventions take seconds. Do any of these?

questions.text: A group of physicians from Rashid Hospital has arrived at the scene of an MCI and is wondering where to go. The best place for a physician to be located is the:
questions.explanation: Physicians add most value treating patients in the treatment area.
questions.hint: Where would a doctor's advanced skills help the most patients at once?

questions.text: In HAZMAT, H stands for:
questions.explanation: HAZMAT = HAZardous MATerials.
questions.hint: Split the word: HAZ + MAT.

questions.text: A mass casualty incident which overwhelms the resources both on-scene and at the receiving facilities/hospitals is the typical definition of:
questions.explanation: When resources at the scene AND at the receiving hospitals are overwhelmed and outside help is needed, the event is a disaster. A multiple casualty incident only exceeds the initial crews.
questions.hint: When even the receiving hospitals are overwhelmed, the whole community needs outside help.

questions.text: Provides the Incident Commander with a risk assessment of the incident action plan:
questions.explanation: Risk assessment is the Safety Officer's role.
questions.hint: Assessing risk is this officer's specialty.

questions.text: In triaging, what are the 3 immediate management steps that can be performed?
questions.explanation: START allows only opening the airway, controlling major bleeding and positioning.
questions.hint: Only quick, life-saving actions. Transport and a full ABC assessment come later.

questions.text: Secondary triaging should be performed in the:
questions.explanation: Patients are re-triaged on arrival in the treatment area.
questions.hint: It happens after patients are moved off the incident site, but before they leave the scene.

questions.text: RPM in triage stands for:
questions.explanation: The three START parameters.
questions.hint: These are the three things START checks after asking who can walk.

questions.text: In responding to any emergency, what is the most important thing to consider?
questions.explanation: Self first, then team, then bystanders, then patient.
questions.hint: An injured rescuer helps no one.

questions.text: In METHANE, T stands for:
questions.explanation: T = Type of incident.
questions.hint: After saying where it is, dispatch needs to know what kind of event this is: crash, fire, explosion…

questions.text: A material or substance that poses a danger and harmful effect to life, property or the environment:
questions.explanation: Definition of hazardous material.
questions.hint: Which option covers solids, liquids and gases that can harm life, property or the environment?

questions.text: Your first responsibility when arriving at an MCI is:
options: Secure that the scene is safe
questions.explanation: Scene safety precedes all patient care.
questions.hint: Nothing else can start until it's safe to work.

questions.text: The START triage system stands for:
questions.explanation: START = Simple Triage And Rapid Treatment.
questions.hint: The first part is the sorting itself; the second part is what you do quickly afterwards.

questions.text: What year was DCAS Crisis and Disaster created?
questions.explanation: Established in 2009.
questions.hint: It's the earliest of the four years listed.

questions.text: Food and clean water are needed for medical responders during an MCI. Which section would be responsible for acquiring these supplies?
questions.explanation: Logistics provides facilities, services, food and supplies.
questions.hint: Which section provides facilities, food and equipment for the responders?

questions.text: In an MCI, disaster buses (especially buses A and C) can be used as:
questions.explanation: They can serve as transport, treatment and surgical space.
questions.hint: Buses A and C each have a surgical room, as well as space to treat and carry patients.

questions.text: In the command structure, BRONZE is considered:
questions.explanation: Gold = strategic, Silver = tactical, Bronze = operational.
questions.hint: Bronze is the level working hands-on at the scene.

questions.text: If someone fails the mental status test, you should tag them:
questions.explanation: Unable to follow simple commands = RED (immediate).
questions.hint: Not being able to follow simple commands means a serious problem that needs care now.

questions.text: You are the first ambulance at the scene. What role will you assume?
questions.explanation: The first-arriving crew assumes command until relieved.
questions.hint: Someone has to take charge from the very first minute.

questions.text: You assumed the role of Incident Commander. When senior staff/the shift in-charge arrives, what will you do?
options: Still assume the Incident Command role
Transfer command and responsibility and transport available patients to hospital
Transfer command and responsibility and act as IC assistant
Assign the shift in-charge to the treatment area
questions.explanation: Formal transfer of command; the former IC stays to assist.
questions.hint: Hand over command, but don't take your knowledge of the scene away with you.

questions.text: In HAZMAT, how can hazardous material enter your body?
options: All routes: injection, ingestion, absorption and inhalation
questions.explanation: All four routes of exposure apply.
questions.hint: Breathing, swallowing, skin and eyes, and penetrating wounds: count the routes.

questions.text: Which of the following best defines a "Mass Casualty Incident"? An MCI is a situation…
options: With major loss of community property and revenue
For which the President declares a disaster area
Where healthcare needs exceed healthcare resources
Caused by an act of global terrorism
questions.explanation: Needs exceeding resources defines an MCI.
questions.hint: An MCI is defined by the gap between patient needs and resources, not by its cause.

questions.text: You are a bystander responding to an explosion. Which of these should you do first?
options: Begin giving first aid to the injured at the scene
Remove debris from the scene that might cause injury
Enter the scene and then communicate with 999 or dispatch
Stop curious onlookers going near the scene
questions.explanation: Prevent more casualties first (secondary devices, collapse); don't enter the scene.
questions.hint: First stop the number of casualties from growing. Think secondary devices and collapse.

questions.text: You are responding to a mass casualty emergency. According to our triage system, victims should initially be grouped according to which of the following?
questions.explanation: START begins by separating those who can walk.
questions.hint: The very first sort in START uses a single voice command.

questions.text: A young lady at a disaster scene who was triaged as a green patient should be:
options: Advised to go to the nearest hospital
Advised to contact her private doctor
Kept at a safe distance from the scene, to be further evaluated
questions.explanation: GREEN patients are held in a safe area for re-triage — conditions can deteriorate.
questions.hint: Patients with minor injuries can still deteriorate.

questions.text: What parameters will you take into consideration to triage victims as BLACK?
questions.explanation: All are injuries/signs incompatible with life.
questions.hint: Which of these are signs of death that no treatment can reverse?

questions.text: This is an example of a crisis:
questions.explanation: All can be crises.
questions.hint: A crisis is any developing unstable or dangerous situation. Check each option against that.

questions.text: At a fire incident, a police officer saw one patient along the hallway of the building and asks you to help. What is your initial action?
options: Immediately help the patient because he needs medical attention
Ask Civil Defense to bring the patient to you
Ignore the policeman because this is not your responsibility
Tell the police officer to get the patient
questions.explanation: Medics don't enter the hot zone; Civil Defense (fire/rescue) extracts the patient.
questions.hint: Who has the protective equipment and training to enter a burning building?

questions.text: Signs that identify the hazardous material contained within a transport vehicle are called:
questions.explanation: Placards display the UN/hazard class on vehicles.
questions.hint: The diamond-shaped or orange signs on the outside of tankers have a specific name.

questions.text: Which patient should be transported first during an MCI?
options: Patient with a broken femur, conscious
80-year-old lady with VS: BP 140/90, RR 20, coherent
questions.explanation: The femur fracture is the highest salvageable priority; the apneic patient is expectant.
questions.hint: Rule out the expectant and the minor patients first. Who is serious but still saveable?

questions.text: In which of the following zones is the EMT expected to be staged at the scene of a hazardous materials incident?
questions.explanation: EMS stages and treats in the cold (support) zone.
questions.hint: EMS works where there is no contamination.

questions.text: Using START triage guidelines, a patient at a mass-casualty incident who is alert and has a capillary refill time of less than 2 seconds is deemed:
questions.explanation: Normal RPM but not ambulatory = YELLOW (delayed).
questions.hint: Breathing, perfusion and mental status are fine, but the question doesn't say the patient can walk.

questions.text: The area in which patients are treated at a multiple-casualty incident (MCI):
questions.explanation: Self-explanatory.
questions.hint: The area is named after what happens there.

questions.text: A 15-year-old boy with a broken arm walking around the scene:
questions.explanation: Ambulatory = GREEN.
questions.hint: Can he walk?

questions.text: A responsive 35-year-old male has pale, moist skin and respirations of 32/min:
questions.explanation: RR > 30 = RED.
questions.hint: Compare the breathing rate with START's cut-off of 30 a minute.

questions.text: An unresponsive male has snoring respirations. His breathing improves when you open his airway:
questions.explanation: Breathes only after airway positioning = RED.
questions.hint: A patient who only breathes properly once you position the airway needs help now.

questions.text: As a Triage Officer at an MCI, you find a patient unconscious, with no obvious injuries and without a carotid pulse. What action will you take?
options: Consider as expectant and go to another patient
Call one ambulance and load this patient immediately
Tag as red and make him your priority
questions.explanation: No CPR in MCI triage — pulseless/apneic = expectant.
questions.hint: During MCI triage, would CPR on one patient be the best use of your time?

questions.text: Which of the following events would MOST likely cause an open, or uncontained, multiple casualty incident?
questions.explanation: A tornado affects a wide, evolving area — the number of victims isn't known up front.
questions.hint: Which event covers a wide area where you can't know at first how many victims there are?

questions.text: A multiple casualty incident is MOST accurately defined as an event in which:
options: Mutual aid from other agencies is required to care for numerous patients
There are more patients who require advanced life support than patients who do not
The number of patients exceeds the resources available to the initial responders
There are at least 25 patients, more than half of whom are critically injured
questions.explanation: Defined by resources, not a number.
questions.hint: It's measured against the first responders' resources, not against a fixed patient count.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a responsibility of the Incident Commander?
options: Developing a plan to manage the incident
questions.explanation: The IC sets objectives, plans and assesses the scene; authorizing specific treatments is medical direction, not command.
questions.hint: The IC manages the incident. Individual clinical decisions sit with the clinicians.

questions.text: During a small-scale incident, the Incident Commander:
options: Delegates all authority to the senior paramedic
Primarily assumes the role of safety officer
May perform all the command functions
Will likely not respond to the scene
questions.explanation: ICS is scalable — on small incidents the IC may cover every function.
questions.hint: The command system scales down as well as up.

questions.text: You are the first responder to an MCI. What is your priority action from the following?
questions.explanation: Size up the scene first; METHANE, backup and triage follow.
questions.hint: You need information before you can triage, report or ask for help.

questions.text: When to activate the Disaster Bus:
options: You have 10 or more RED patients
You have 10 or more yellow patients
You have 10 or more green patients
questions.explanation: Any category reaching 10+ patients triggers bus activation.
questions.hint: The trigger is the number of patients in a category, whatever the colour.

questions.text: He has the authority and responsibility to stop a rescuer if he believes that he is in danger:
questions.explanation: The Safety Officer can halt unsafe acts immediately.
questions.hint: This officer can halt unsafe work on the spot.

questions.text: At an MCI, staff from Khaleej News approach you and ask for an interview regarding the incident. What is your appropriate action?
options: Answer the questions in a polite manner
Instruct him to contact the CEO
Direct him to talk to the Information Officer
questions.explanation: All media enquiries go to the Public Information Officer.
questions.hint: All media questions go to one designated person.

questions.text: As a Staging Officer, you are responsible for:
options: Advising the Incident Commander that the patient is already transported
Making sure that all patients have been triaged
Advising the Incident Commander of the status of resources
Advising the Treatment Officer when and where to transport the patients
questions.explanation: Staging tracks available resources and reports to the IC.
questions.hint: Staging manages the ambulances and crews waiting to be used.

questions.text: When responding to a car accident, the proper way to approach a driver trapped inside the car is from the front. Why?
options: You can see and feel if the car engine is running
For you to see if there is a car from behind
To prevent him from turning his head sideways
questions.explanation: Approaching from the front keeps the patient looking straight ahead, protecting the C-spine.
questions.hint: Think about the patient's neck.

questions.text: When responding to a road traffic accident, what is the most important equipment to bring?
questions.explanation: Trauma-focused kit: responder bag, backboard, carevent and C-collar.
questions.hint: Pick the set that covers trauma: airway and breathing support plus spinal motion restriction.

questions.text: As Incident Commander, what designation will you assign to the 2nd ambulance unit that arrives?
questions.explanation: DCAS protocol: the second unit takes Staging and Treatment.
questions.hint: The first crew already covers command and triage. Which two jobs are still uncovered?

questions.text: When you arrive at an MCI as a backup ambulance, you will directly report to the:
questions.explanation: Arriving units report to the IC (or staging when established) for assignment.
questions.hint: Arriving units check in with whoever is in charge to get an assignment.

questions.text: Which of the following patients requires KED extrication?
options: RED patient suspected of spinal injury
GREEN agile patient trapped inside the car
Stable, conversant patient seated in the car who is unable to move his lower extremities
RED patient lying on the ground
questions.explanation: Short spinal devices (KED) are for stable, seated patients with suspected spinal injury. Unstable RED patients need rapid extrication, and a walking GREEN patient with no spinal concern doesn't need a KED.
questions.hint: The KED takes time to apply. Which patient is stable enough to wait for it and still needs spinal protection?

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT the role of the first-arriving EMT at the scene of a possible hazardous materials emergency?
options: Rescuing any victims still in the area of the spill
questions.explanation: Entry and rescue in the hot zone is for trained HAZMAT teams.
questions.hint: Which action needs protective equipment and HAZMAT training?

questions.text: In most cases, the only reason for which the remains of the dead should be moved during the initial triage phase of an MCI is to:
options: Allow family members to view the body
Obtain access to a possible living victim
Obtain a positive identification of the victim
questions.explanation: Bodies stay in place (evidence/ID) unless blocking access to the living.
questions.hint: Bodies are evidence and help identification. What single reason justifies moving one early?

questions.text: A 50-year-old man has bilateral fractured femurs. He has a faint radial pulse, a respiratory rate of 24 and follows commands. By START criteria he is:
questions.explanation: By strict START: cannot walk, RR under 30, radial pulse present and follows commands = YELLOW. Watch closely and re-triage — bilateral femur fractures can cause shock and he may soon become RED..)
questions.hint: Go through RPM strictly: breathing rate, radial pulse, then commands. The injuries alone don't decide the colour.

questions.text: START is a system that relies on simple commands and which 3 physiological parameters?
questions.explanation: RPM: respiration, pulse/perfusion, mental status.
questions.hint: These are the R, P and M of RPM.

questions.text: What colour TARP in the treatment area should be placed close to the loading/transportation area?
questions.explanation: RED patients leave first, so their tarp is nearest the loading zone.
questions.hint: Which patients leave the scene first?

questions.text: Sector officer responsible for collecting the destination control/tracking number:
questions.explanation: Transport tracks each patient's destination.
questions.hint: Which officer knows where each patient went?

questions.text: Sector officer responsible for liaising with other stakeholders:
questions.explanation: Coordinating with other stakeholders is on the IC checklist.
questions.hint: Coordinating with other stakeholders sits with whoever is in overall charge.

questions.text: Ideally, the first ambulance on scene will be the:
options: Transport officer because he knows the location
First ambulance to transport the RED patient
Last ambulance to leave the scene
questions.explanation: The first crew becomes command and stays until the incident closes.
questions.hint: The first crew takes command. When does command leave the scene?
